person.owns: one exact persistent individual when identity is causally relevant

team.owns: one exact named roster and its small-group doctrine, leadership and assignments

force.owns: conserved manpower, troop pools, broad readiness and institutional military capacity

formation.owns: one explicit operational allocation drawn from a force, including current composition, readiness, cohesion, morale, location and command attachments

cohort.owns: compressed state for similar unnamed people until exact identity matters

manpower_invariant: A force is the single manpower-accounting authority. Explicit formation personnel are a subset of the force deployed partition and can never exceed it. Named people or teams embedded in a formation are included in that formation headcount rather than added on top.
team_invariant: A team is an exact social and tactical roster. Large forces do not need one persistent team object for every ordinary squad; unnamed squad structure remains implicit in force composition and doctrine until identity matters.
formation_invariant: A formation is the operational mass-combat actor. Split, merge, reinforcement, reconstitution and release conserve personnel and material claims. A formation may be represented at whatever size is useful for the current operation.
commander_rule: A commander is a separate exact person. Command authority changes control and coordination, never ownership of aggregate manpower and never the commander's personal physical statistics into soldier averages.
support_rule: Support personnel and formations contribute only capabilities justified by their troop pools, doctrine, equipment and current assignment. They remain casualty-bearing and targetable when committed.
large_war_rule: A 10,000-person army is represented by a force commitment and a bounded set of operational formations. Important exact teams may be attached as subsets of those formations without double-counting their members. Ordinary squads stay aggregate unless a local causal event requires them to materialize.
